clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old male presented with polyuria, polydipsia, weakness, pallor, and signs of severe hyperglycemia alongside a history of bilateral progressive hearing loss and no weight gain for 3 years. Clinical examination revealed short stature, hallux valgus, hyperpigmented skin plaques, Boutonniere deformities, scrotal mass with small penis and enclosed testicles, absence of pubic and axillary hair, and hematological abnormalities. These multisystem features clinically supported a diagnosis of H syndrome. A mutation analysis of the SLC29A3 gene was ordered for molecular confirmation, but the result was not documented in the available clinical data.
